description: Read one incident in full, with every alert sent for it. It has id, monitor_id or heartbeat_id (exactly one is set), started_at, resolved_at, cause, cause_detail, last_notified_at, acknowledged_at, acknowledged_by, acknowledged_via, acknowledged_by_label, renotify_count and notification_logs (each alert attempt: id, channel_type, destination, event TRIGGERED or RESOLVED, sent_at, status PENDING, SENT or FAILED, and error; SSL alerts (SSL_EXPIRY, SSL_RENEWAL_OVERDUE, SSL_COVERAGE_LOST), change alerts (CHANGE_DETECTED) and domain alerts (DOMAIN_EXPIRY, DOMAIN_ON_HOLD, DOMAIN_NOT_IN_REGISTRY) are not tied to an incident and never appear here). Use it to tell whether its alerts were delivered and who acknowledged it: acknowledged_by is the Fettle user's uuid (null for a Telegram tap), acknowledged_via the source (DASHBOARD, API_KEY, MCP or TELEGRAM; null when unacknowledged or acknowledged before the source was recorded) and acknowledged_by_label the actor that is not a Fettle user (the Telegram name, the API key name or the MCP client name). MCP means acknowledged through the remote Fettle MCP endpoint (label: the connected app's name, or the API key's name when that connection uses a key); the stdio fettle-mcp package and any REST call with an API key record API_KEY (label: the key's name). For the person's name and email use get_incident_context. destination is an email address, a Telegram chat id, or only scheme://host/… of a webhook. To find incidents use list_incidents; to stop its reminders use acknowledge_incident.

incident_id.description: The incident's uuid from list_incidents. An id that is not an incident of this organization is a 404.

name: get_incident

anyOf.description: Known values: DASHBOARD, API_KEY, MCP, TELEGRAM.

cause.description: Known values: TIMEOUT, DNS_FAILURE, CONNECTION_REFUSED, TLS_INVALID, HTTP_4XX, HTTP_5XX, HTTP_UNEXPECTED_STATUS, KEYWORD_MISSING, TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS, TARGET_BLOCKED, PORT_STATE_MISMATCH, INVALID_TARGET, HEARTBEAT_MISSED, HEARTBEAT_FAILED, UNKNOWN.

channel_type.description: Known values: EMAIL, TELEGRAM, WEBHOOK, SLACK, DISCORD.

event.description: Known values: TRIGGERED, RESOLVED, SSL_EXPIRY, SSL_RENEWAL_OVERDUE, SSL_COVERAGE_LOST, CHANGE_DETECTED, DOMAIN_EXPIRY, DOMAIN_ON_HOLD, DOMAIN_NOT_IN_REGISTRY.

title: Get an incident
